source.title: Neural sampling from cognitive maps enables goal-directed imagination and planning

confidence_rationale: Strong formal analogue for ARC-018: a learned cognitive map plus a state-difference-to-action inverse model plus stochastic virtual action selection generates goal-directed imagined trajectories, including spatial rerouting, abstract graph paths, and compositional silhouette decomposition. Marked mixed rather than supports because it is a simulation/model paper, not direct biological evidence, and because it leaves ARC-018's REE-specific gaps untouched: E2 action-object indexing, live E2 fidelity, and harm/goal error updating.
failure_signatures: If REE's cognitive-map substrate lacks any reliable state-difference-to-action inverse readout, it will miss the core GCML mechanism that turns a map into goal-directed imagined action sequences.

If stochastic proposal generation is unconstrained by map geometry, it is not the GCML/Pfeiffer-style mechanism; useful randomness should remain goal-directed and self-correcting rather than pure trajectory noise.
If a future ARC-018 validation treats this paper as direct biological support, it overclaims; the source only supports formal plausibility and benchmark behavior.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A generative cognitive map learner using learned forward structure, a state-difference-to-action inverse model, stochastic virtual action selection, and compositional coding can sample goal-directed imagined trajectories in spatial, abstract-graph, and compositional task spaces with low replanning cost.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-018's hippocampal rollout loop should be read as a map-guided stochastic proposal generator, not brute-force search. The strongest transferable form is: current/goal difference in the map -> inverse action readout -> internally predicted next state -> repeat, with controlled noise producing a diverse but goal-directed candidate set.
mapping.mapping_caveat: GCML is an engineered model inspired by hippocampal/grid-cell evidence. It does not prove the biological hippocampus uses this exact algorithm, and it does not validate REE's E2 action-object coordinate or harm-specific viability map. It is therefore a formal/computational bridge, not scored biological confirmation.
mapping.source_context: Open-access Nature Machine Intelligence article; code repository LH-cbicr/GCML contains notebooks for grid-cell, abstract-graph, and tiling benchmarks; Zenodo software citation in the paper.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality model paper with code and broad benchmark coverage. Mapping fidelity is high at the algorithmic-form level but capped because ARC-018's controversial parts are REE-specific: action-object map coordinates and harm/goal error updates.
